entities.summary: Anthony Henday was one of the first Europeans to explore the interior of what would eventually become western Canada. He ventured farther into the interior of western Canada than any European had before him. As an employee of the Hudson's Bay Company, he travelled across the prairies in the 1750s, journeyed into what is now central Alberta, and possibly arrived at the present site of Red Deer. He camped along the North Saskatchewan River, perhaps on the present site of Rocky Mountain House or Edmonton, and is said to have been the first European to see the Rocky Mountains, if only from a distance.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Anthony Henday's journey into western Canada marked a significant regional milestone, as he was the first European to see the Rocky Mountains from a distance and explored parts of what is now central Alberta. His travels expanded the Hudson's Bay Company's territory and contributed to the early mapping of the region.
